How to test your microphone

Five seconds to a useful answer.

You do not need an account or a download. Connect your microphone, allow access, and use the meter and short recording to check it before a Zoom, Teams, Meet, or Discord call.

  1. 01

    Click the test button

    Start the test when you are ready to give this page microphone access.

  2. 02

    Allow microphone access

    Choose Allow in your browser prompt. The browser controls when a site can use your mic.

  3. 03

    Speak and watch the meter

    Say a few words at your normal volume. The level bars should move as you speak.

  4. 04

    Switch input devices if needed

    Use the device list to select your headset, USB microphone, or another available input.

  5. 05

    Record a short clip

    Play the local recording back to check how your voice actually sounds.

Microphone FAQs

How do I test my microphone?

Find quick answers for how to test a microphone online, on Windows 10 and 11, on a PC, Mac, laptop, Microsoft Teams, or with AirPods.

How to test microphone online?+

Click Start microphone test, allow microphone access when your browser asks, and speak normally. The live meter should move as your microphone picks up sound. You can also record a short clip and play it back locally.

How to test if microphone is working?+

Start the microphone test, allow browser access, and speak into the microphone. If the level meter responds and a recorded clip plays back clearly, the microphone is working. If there is no signal, check the selected input, mute switch, and device connection.

How to test microphone Windows 10?+

To test microphone Windows 10, open Settings, choose System, then Sound, and select your microphone under Input to check the input level. You can also use this online microphone test: click Start microphone test, allow access, speak, and confirm that the live meter responds.

How to test microphone Windows 11?+

To test microphone Windows 11, open Settings, go to System, then Sound, and choose your microphone under Input. Test the signal, or click Start microphone test on this page and speak to see the live level meter respond.

How to test microphone on Mac?+

To test microphone on Mac, open System Settings, select Sound, and choose the microphone under Input. You can also use this page to allow browser access, watch the live meter, and play back a short local recording.

How to test microphone on laptop?+

Make sure the laptop microphone is not muted, click Start microphone test, and allow access in your browser. Speak at a normal volume and confirm that the level meter moves. If you use a headset or USB microphone, select it from the input device list.

How to test microphone in Teams and Zoom?+

Open Microsoft Teams or Zoom Settings, choose Audio/Devices, select your microphone, and run the test call. You can test the same microphone here first by checking the live meter and local recording.

How to test AirPods or wireless microphone?+

Connect your AirPods or Bluetooth headset, choose them as the input device, and click Start microphone test. Speak normally and confirm the live meter moves, then record a 5-second clip to hear playback quality.

How do I test my microphone to hear what other people hear?+

Connect headphones, click Start microphone test, and turn on the 'Hear myself' loopback monitor. You will hear your voice in real time with zero latency, allowing you to check background noise, echo, and volume balance.

Why is my microphone not working?+

Check browser permission, the selected input device, the physical mute switch, and the cable or Bluetooth connection. Close other apps that may be locking the microphone, then reload this page and try again.

Can I test my microphone without uploading audio?+

Yes. This microphone test processes the live stream locally in your browser using the Web Audio API. Audio is never sent to any server, and recordings remain completely private on your device.

How do I test my PC microphone locally without opening Windows sound settings?+

Open TestYourMicrophone.com in your browser. It uses the Web Audio API to test your microphone locally on your device with a live decibel (dBFS) meter, pitch detector, and instant playback with zero configuration required.

Your microphone stream stays on this page.

Microphone access starts only after you click the test button and approve the browser prompt. Level analysis and recordings happen locally in your browser. Stop the test when you are done; the page stops its audio tracks and does not upload your recording.
